title: Keith Richards Rocks a 65-Year-Old Blues Song for Grand Theft Auto VI
summary: Have you ever played a song that's older than your grandparents? Keith Richards just did. The Rolling Stones guitarist recorded his own version of "Bright Lights, Big City," a blues song from 1961 by Jimmy Reed. It's for Grand Theft Auto VI: The Album, the soundtrack for the huge video game. The album has 34 songs and comes out November 19. The game is set in a fictional world called Vice City and Leonida. The original song was sung by Jimmy Reed with a smooth, swinging feel. Richards plays the guitar a little harder and sings with a shaky, trembling voice — a style he's famous for. Where Reed played a harmonica solo, Richards just keeps playing straight through to the end. Richards didn't say when or where he recorded it. Maybe it was during sessions for the Rolling Stones' recent albums, Foreign Tongues or Hackney Diamonds. Either way, he's been busy. Rolling Stone magazine praised his song "Tell Me Straight" from Hackney Diamonds, calling it taut and shadowy. They also loved "Some of Us" from Foreign Tongues, calling it a moving declaration of devotion. The Stones aren't touring in 2026, but Richards told Uncut magazine he could see the band doing a residency somewhere — maybe London, New York, Paris, or Rome. "It's the traveling that takes it out of you," he said. So even at 82, Richards keeps making music. Not bad for a guy whose band started in 1962!
why_it_matters: It shows that music can jump between generations — a song from 1961 can end up in a game kids play today, and an 82-year-old can still be creating something brand new.

background_read: Keith Richards (the guitarist of the Rolling Stones, a British rock band that started playing together in 1962) has been making music for more than 60 years.

Jimmy Reed (an American blues singer from the 1950s and '60s) first sang "Bright Lights, Big City"; blues music began in Black communities in the southern United States and later helped create rock and roll.
Big video games like Grand Theft Auto often pay real musicians to make songs just for the game, so millions of players end up hearing them.
Article_Structure: WHO: Keith Richards, the guitarist of the Rolling Stones, covering a 1961 song by Jimmy Reed
WHAT: He recorded his own version of "Bright Lights, Big City" for Grand Theft Auto VI: The Album, a 34-song soundtrack coming out November 19
WHERE: The game is set in the made-up world of Vice City and Leonida; Richards did not say where he recorded the song
WHY: It shows an 82-year-old rock star still making new music, and he hinted the Stones might do a residency in a city like London, New York, Paris, or Rome

perspectives.description: They are excited that Keith Richards is still recording and playing guitar at 82, and hope it means the band has more music or live shows coming.
They look forward to a huge 34-song album tied to Grand Theft Auto VI, with famous artists making music just for the game.
They are glad a 1961 song will reach a new, younger audience, though some might feel the original by Jimmy Reed is still the one to beat.
